To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
MyosinII contractility is required to maintain platelet structure during collagen‐induced platelet spreading.
myosinIIA is required for maintenance and stabilization of platelet spreading and platelet thrombus stability on collagen.
myosinII is required for platelet spreading on collagen and thrombus stability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of myosin II in platelet function.
the role played by myosinII in thrombus formation.
the molecular and cellular mechanisms of platelet adhesion to collagen and the role of these interactions in thrombus formation and stability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
myosinII is a critical regulator of thrombus growth and stability.
myosinII is important for thrombus formation.
MyosinIIA contractility contributes to platelet spreading on collagen and to thrombus stability, and that this may be important in the context of thrombus embolism and stability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

ROCK inhibition causes a reduction in thrombus growth and stability on collagen, presumably as a result of the loss of myosinIIs in the platelet cytoskeleton, which leads to a loss of contractility and platelet integrity.
myosinIIA is required for platelet stability and thrombus growth.
myosinII contractility is essential for the maintenance of platelet integrity on collagen and that myosinIIs may contribute to thrombus stability in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
myosinII contractility is required to maintain platelet structure on collagen, but not to initiate spreading.
myosinII contractility in spread platelets is required for the maintenance of platelet structural integrity and contributes to thrombosis stability.
the contractile machinery is important in the maintenance of platelet integrity and thrombus stability.
